about.title: About
about.heading: About Logia
about.dek: A free, open library of Christian commentary, set verse by verse beside Scripture.
steps: A page scan on archive.org or a transcription on CCEL, published in 1930 or earlier.
The page Logia copies from is kept in the repository, with its address and when it was fetched.
A script finds each excerpt in its source: word for word, or in runs of six words for a scan.
Where a scan misread the printed page, the fix is a pair kept in the open data.
The excerpt appears on Logia beside the verse it comments on, linked to the full text.
about.fix: A correction from {work}'s scan, one of {n}
about.steps_note: Every one of the {n} excerpts goes through these steps; {fixes} scan misreadings are corrected in all.
body: Logia sets each verse of the Bible beside what the church has said about it, from the early church to the 1800s. It is free to read, free to share, and its data is open for anyone to build on, in the spirit of Sefaria's library of Jewish texts.
The name comes from *ta logia tou theou*, “the oracles of God” (Romans 3:2), and from Papias's lost *Exposition of the Logia of the Lord*, one of the first Christian commentaries.

Every excerpt is copied from a public-domain edition, never rewritten, and the source text it came from is kept beside it. A script checks each excerpt against its source on every change: word for word for a transcription, and in runs of six words for a page scan, whose lines carry margin notes and running heads. Where a scan misread a letter (“Let ns” for “Let us”), the correction is listed openly and applied when the site is built.

Logia reads the Open Word Bible, a CC0 translation from Hebrew and Greek with the reasoning behind every sentence. Logia never edits it: it is imported at a pinned version from the Open Word Bible's own repository.

Logia starts in English. Each new language is translated from the best public-domain source, the original Greek, Latin or German where that is better than the English, and reviewed by native speakers before it is marked reviewed.
Logia's data and writing are CC0, its code is MIT, and everything is on GitHub.
